new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel-native/src/host.rs:918-923 (configured program checked with is_file against the current directory), :579 (Command::new(&self.program))
new_findings.evidence: An embedder that passes a bare file name (Av1WorkerOptions::program = "reel-native-av1-worker.exe") passes the is_file check against the CURRENT directory, but on Windows std resolves a bare file name by search: child PATH (none after env_clear), the application directory, System32, the Windows directory, then the parent PATH (read in rust-src of the local stable 1.91.1, library/std/src/sys/process/windows.rs resolve_exe/search_paths; the workspace pins 1.97.1 whose rust-src is not installed, UNVERIFIED for that exact version). The file checked and the file executed can differ, and a same-named binary on PATH can run as the decoder worker (HELLO checks only self-reported strings). Default discovery is fixed; this is the caller-supplied override only, and the same shape exists in the motion-js and score-plugin copies (D18). Not a regression of 7886369.
new_findings.remediation: Optional, cheap: at construction make the configured program absolute (std::path::absolute, or join a bare name to the executable directory) and is_file that path; refuse a bare name otherwise; one unit test. Fold into D18 if preferred

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel-native/src/host.rs:1045 (segment_wall set before checkout), :615 (HELLO wall = deadline_after(spawn_timeout) only)
new_findings.evidence: The HELLO wait is cancellable and bounded, but by spawn_timeout alone; a caller with segment_deadline < spawn_timeout can exceed its segment deadline by up to spawn_timeout while a worker starts. Defaults (10 s vs 300 s) never hit it. Pre-existing semantics (the old recv_timeout used the same bound).
new_findings.remediation: Optional: wall = deadline_after(spawn_timeout).min(segment_wall) by passing the segment wall into checkout/spawn

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/video.rs:265-272 (Forward holds no declared track size), :293-324 (accept: :302 planes_match_format compares the picture only with its own format; :316-319 copies every plane into `packed`; only then :320 compares with max_chunk_bytes); the declared VideoTrack width/height exist (video.rs:433-434, passed to the external decoder) but never reach Forward
new_findings.evidence: Register PLR-032 (lane SMB-REEL-AV1-ROUTE, disposition FIX_LANE 'refuse as DecoderFault::Protocol before packing', carried since R5) is unfixed at HEAD, and the lane deferred it explicitly (lane next: 'NOT in this pass: PLR-032'). Effect: a registered ExternalVideoDecoder (any embedder decoder; the reel-native worker is bounded by its declared-size reply cap, host.rs:1046, a generic decoder is not) can return a picture larger than the container-declared size: up to max_chunk_bytes it is delivered with dimensions the probe never reported, and above it the whole picture is copied into a second buffer before LimitExceeded (transient 2x; V4-02 'check bounds before allocating'). R7-review-b kept PLR-032 PLAUSIBLE, but raised the other three carried FIX_LANE items of these two lanes (PLR-033, PLR-034, PLR-035) to CONFIRMED FAILs; this lane has one verdict left before CX-EXEC-015(1) fix_budget_exhausted.
new_findings.remediation: Carry the declared (width, height) into Forward; when declared (non-zero), a picture whose format.width/height exceed them is DecoderFault::Protocol (use <=, not ==, so frame-size changes within the sequence maximum stay legal); compute the packed size as a checked sum of plane lengths and refuse > max_chunk_bytes before any extend_from_slice. Tests: a lying fake decoder returning (a) a picture larger than the declared track -> Protocol with an empty sink, (b) an oversize picture -> LimitExceeded before packing. ALTERNATIVE: the lead records a WAIVE/DEFER lead_decision for PLR-032 in workflow/plausible-register.json before the lane is offered; then the lane is SAFE_TO_JUDGE.

new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/registry.rs:236-265 (a layout-usable proxy is decoded and its error returned), video.rs:403-405 (choose() None -> CodecUnavailable before any packet is read); pinned by tests/video_route.rs block 'Same, nothing registered'
new_findings.evidence: Behaviour change from 8438b1d: with prefer=Proxy, a Trusted original, a default (Untrusted) proxy and no external decoder, the whole request is CodecUnavailable although the original alone would decode (in-process, feature av1); before, the proxy was decoded in-process (the defect). Not a safety problem. An unusable proxy (stale grant, probe error) falls back to the original (ProxyUnusableUsedOriginal), an undecodable-under-its-trust proxy does not; the code docs (registry.rs:204-207) do not state this, only the lane notes do. Spec text on proxy fallback NOT_INSPECTED.
new_findings.remediation: Either decide before decoding (choose() for the proxy track is None) and fall back to the original with ProxyNote::ProxyUnusableUsedOriginal (safe: the refusal happens before any packet reaches the sink), or state the no-fallback rule in decode_segment_routed's doc

new_findings.evidence: 'The source is SourceTrust::Untrusted: compressed video goes to the registered external decoder or is CodecUnavailable'. Since 8438b1d a ProxySource built with with_trust(SourceTrust::Trusted) keeps its own trust in decode_segment too (registry.rs:193-201 -> :242-251), so its AV1 reaches in-process rav1d with feature av1. Behaviour follows the stated policy (the caller vouched for that proxy); the doc sentence is now incomplete.
new_findings.remediation: Reword: 'The ORIGINAL is SourceTrust::Untrusted; a proxy keeps its own ProxySource::trust'
